articles.body:
A complete chain lets someone else trust that the item is what it claims to be. Gaps, such as examining before receipt, weaken it.

articles.title: Chain of custody

articles.body:
A clock running fast shows a later time than reality: subtract. Slow: add. UTC is the common reference used in every case.

*This is a simplified explanation for learning, not official guidance.*
articles.title: Clock offsets and time zones
articles.answer: Devices and systems record time differently. Correct known offsets and time zones before you compare events.

articles.title: Corroboration and independent sources
articles.answer: A point is stronger when independent sources agree. Copies of one record count as one source.

articles.body:
Investafiction is built around these four ideas: originals stay sealed, opening one needs a reason, every action is logged, and your case lead sets the scope. They are inspired by widely used UK digital evidence principles.

*This is a simplified explanation for learning, not official guidance.*
articles.title: Digital evidence principles
articles.answer: Do not change data that may be relied on; if you must access originals, be competent and explain why; keep a record of everything; the person in charge makes sure the rules are followed.
questions: what are the digital evidence principles

articles.body:
Labelling honestly is part of the analysis mark. Overclaiming, such as calling an inference a fact, can trigger a trap. Statements from witnesses are evidence of what they said, not automatically of what happened.

*This is a simplified explanation for learning, not official guidance.*
articles.title: Fact, inference and assumption
articles.answer: A fact is what the evidence shows directly. An inference is a conclusion that follows from evidence. An assumption is accepted without evidence and must be labelled.

articles.body:
Location, dates, writing style and connections help rule matches in or out. Linking the wrong account can mislead a whole enquiry.

*This is a simplified explanation for learning, not official guidance.*
articles.title: False matches
articles.answer: The same name, handle or photo can belong to different people or businesses. Check other details before linking them.

articles.body:
Source: A always reliable, B mostly reliable, C sometimes reliable, D unreliable, E untested. Information: 1 known true without reservation, 2 known personally to the source, 3 not known personally but corroborated, 4 cannot be judged, 5 suspected false.

*This is a simplified explanation for learning, not official guidance.*
articles.title: Source and information grading
articles.answer: Grade the source (how reliable it has been) and the information (how likely it is to be true) separately.

articles.body:
Investafiction uses SHA-256. Matching hashes show a copy is identical to the original it was checked against.

*This is a simplified explanation for learning, not official guidance.*
articles.title: Hashes
articles.answer: A hash is a fixed-length fingerprint of a file. Change one byte and the hash changes completely.

articles.body:
Each case follows the same loop: brief, collect within scope, grade, analyse, report, and act on new material at each stage. The program draws on the National Intelligence Model's ideas in simplified form.

*This is a simplified explanation for learning, not official guidance.*
articles.title: The intelligence process
articles.answer: Information is collected, evaluated (graded), analysed and turned into an assessment that informs decisions, then reviewed as new information arrives.

articles.body:
Ask: is there a less intrusive way? Am I collecting about people with no link to the question? Is the period as short as it can be?

*This is a simplified explanation for learning, not official guidance.*
articles.title: Necessity and proportionality
articles.answer: Necessary means the step helps answer the tasking. Proportionate means it is no more intrusive than it needs to be.

articles.body:
Scope, continuity, proportionality, careful capture, honest labelling and fair treatment of witnesses all appear as traps.

*This is a simplified explanation for learning, not official guidance.*
articles.title: Why procedure matters
articles.answer: Good procedure keeps evidence reliable and people treated fairly. The traps in each case reward the habits real analysts rely on.

articles.body:
Even public material should be collected only when it is relevant and proportionate. Repeated, focused viewing of one person's profile can need authority too.

*This is a simplified explanation for learning, not official guidance.*
articles.title: Public and private information
articles.answer: Public pages can be viewed and captured. Private material needs specific authority, and using a false identity to reach it is deception.

articles.body:
Ask what the item actually shows, and whether anything contradicts your theory before you rely on it.

articles.title: Red herrings and noise
articles.answer: Every case includes irrelevant items and misleading leads, as real cases do. Following one into your report costs marks.

articles.body:
Record the conflict, look for data that resolves it, and say what remains unverified. Only say someone gave a false account where evidence directly contradicts them and they must have known.

*This is a simplified explanation for learning, not official guidance.*
articles.title: Witness accounts and memory
articles.answer: Honest witnesses misremember times, places and details. A difference between accounts is something to explain, not proof of a lie.

2. Select a claim and choose a relation: **agrees with**, **conflicts with**, **adds detail to**, **cannot be checked**, **supported by evidence** or **contradicted by evidence**.

1. Install Node.js and Rust (rustup).

articles.answer: One go at a case. Each case can be attempted many times.

articles.answer: The in-case time, which advances while you work.

articles.title: Case lead
articles.answer: The person who tasks you and sends messages as the case develops.

articles.title: Case pack
articles.answer: A .invcase file containing one complete case.

articles.title: CDR

articles.answer: A reference to the evidence that supports a finding, such as EV-012.

articles.title: Clock offset
articles.answer: How far a device's clock is fast or slow compared with true time.

articles.title: Collateral intrusion

articles.title: Confidence

articles.answer: Favouring evidence that fits your theory and ignoring what does not.

articles.title: Continuity gap

articles.answer: Support for a point from an independent source.

articles.title: Countersignature
articles.answer: A second approval needed above a set limit.

articles.title: Cross reference
articles.answer: A link between files in a pack that must point to something that exists.

articles.title: Custody

articles.title: Debrief

articles.title: Deception

articles.title: Deleted entry
